goal: A quick-turnaround (~25-40 min) TRM Sudoku baseline to A/B LUT swaps in Phase B. Lower final accuracy than the full 5h run is acceptable; the point is a stable, repeatable signal that still exercises the recursion + deep supervision.
based_on: exp_a01_stock_trm_sudoku_baseline (same reference repo/optimizer); this is a deliberately cheaper config, not stock.

arch.note: cheaper recursion: H_cycles*(L_cycles+1)=8 forward evals/step vs stock 21 (H=3,L=6) -> ~2.5x faster/step and less activation memory (lets batch go to 768).

optim.optimizer: AdamATan2 (pure-PyTorch drop-in adam_atan2.py; identical math to the fused kernel; a=b=1, decoupled WD)

data.train: FULL augmented train (symlinked): Sudoku-Extreme 1000 subsample x 1000 aug (unchanged)
data.test: SUBSAMPLED to 5000 puzzles (first 5k of the 422,786 test set) via subsample_test.py -> each eval is ~7 batches (seconds) instead of ~826 (minutes)

deviations_from_stock: recursion H_cycles 3->2, L_cycles 6->3 (cheaper; caps accuracy lower)
eval on a 5000-puzzle test subset instead of the full 422,786
batch 768 (stock; the cheaper recursion frees the memory the full run lacked)
AdamATan2 pure-PyTorch drop-in (Blackwell sm_120; see exp_a01)

expected.val_exact_accuracy: ~40-60% (well below the paper's 87.4%; this is a fast A/B baseline, not a fidelity run)
